33749432.extract:
Lead Section:
Second-Ponce de Leon Baptist Church is a prominent church in the Garden Hills section of Buckhead, Atlanta, founded in 1854 as Second Baptist Church. It merged with two other churches in 1932 to form the modern-day church. The church's mission is to "take the whole gospel to the whole person," as demonstrated by Jesus during His ministry on earth. It is a community engagement and spiritual growth hub in Atlanta.

Main Body:
1. History: The church evolved from Second Baptist Church, established in 1854, to the current church.
2. Location: Located at 2715 Peachtree Road NE, it is a significant landmark in the Buckhead community.
3. Significance: The church plays a crucial role in the community, focusing on community engagement and spiritual growth.
4. Notable Events: Notable events include the purchase of property in 1947 for a new church on Wieuca Road.
5. Notable Figures: Pastor and staff members contribute to the church's mission and community impact.

17 Welcome to Second-Ponce! 

We are a family of Christian believers on the brink of newness in the life of our congregation ... new joys, 

new ideas, new faces and new opportunities to serve God and our community. Admittedly, we’re in a 

space that fills us with possibility, but we also have a sense of uncertainty. Change is never easy, but we 

are ready to stretch ourselves and explore new methods to reach our community for Christ. 

# From the 

# Pastor Search Committee 

We are in the process of accepting resumes, evaluating credentials and having conversations about 

potential candidates. Calling a new Senior Pastor is a commitment that will define how Second-Ponce 

participates in the eternal family of God. And so here we are ... mindful of the road but enjoying the 

journey. 

Before reading further, know that we have prayed for you as a possible candidate to lead our church. We 

ask that you pray for us as we seek God’s will. 

How It Started 

After more than a decade of service, our previous Senior Pastor shared a desire to simplify his ministry 

and transition to a smaller congregation, a change that would support a slower pace in the next phase of 

life. The anxiety of this news was heightened by the departure of our Associate Pastor who accepted a 

senior pastorate of his own only a few months earlier. In spite of the upheaval, and thanks to our 

courageous and dedicated staff and leadership, we soon got to work seizing the opportunity to set a new 

course for Second-Ponce. 

As a congregation, our first steps forward were a series of deliberate and strategic actions to fill ministry 

gaps and begin the search process. The Executive Committee of the Deacons was tasked with finding an 

Interim Senior Pastor and the church body confirmed a Pastor Search Committee. As that committee, 

we led the congregation through an assessment process of surveys and listening sessions and then began 

crafting a profile of our church and its future leader. What you are about to read is the fruit of that work. 

What Happened Next 

Where We Are Now 

In Hopeful Prayer, 

The Second-Ponce Pastor Search Committee

# Hi! We’re the Pastor Search Committee 

We invite anyone following God’s call to a new place of ministry 

leadership to read our church profile and consider a future at Second-

2Using Technology for Ministry Growth 

In the 1930's, soon after our formation, we 

began a radio broadcasting ministry. In 1962, 

our first worship service telecast premiered. 

Today, our TV ministry continues and has 

expanded to livestreaming on multiple 

platforms. 

In the last 93 years, we have experienced milestones that remain threads in our 

church tapestry. Below, we’ve shared a few highlights from ministry areas that remain 

priorities for Second-Ponce. Scan or click this code to see more landmark occasions 

in the life of our church. 

Built on Relationships 

Modern-day Second-Ponce was formed when three Buckhead churches merged. The first, Second Baptist 

Church, was founded in 1854. During the Civil War, it was spared from being burned due to the efforts of 

Father Thomas O’Reilly who was the Catholic priest at the nearby Immaculate Conception Church. In 

1929, the second and third founding churches, Ponce de Leon Avenue Baptist and Buckhead Baptist, 

merged and moved to the corner of Peachtree and East Wesley Roads where SPdL sits today. Three years 

later, on November 18, 1932, the merger of Second Baptist with Ponce de Leon Baptist Church birthed 

Second-Ponce. 

3

Supporting Churches & Church Starts 

Since 1951, SPdL has started churches and 

fnancially supported the creation of new 

congregations across Atlanta. Recently, we 

increased our geographical footprint in this 

area by supporting a church in Blairsville, 

Georgia, nearly two hours outside of Atlanta. 

Working Toward Racial Reconciliation 

In 2018, we curated a 4-part series, “Use Me, 

God,” about the intersection of race and faith. 

The event marked the 50th anniversary of the 

assassination of Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, 

Jr. Speakers included Ambassador Andrew 

Young and author Taylor Branch. 

Bridging Gaps in Community Services 

In 2022, we partnered with the Cathedral of 

Christ the King to create a new preschool, 

CTK Preschool at Second-Ponce. The school, 

operating from our campus, continues to 

exceed enrollment expectations.

# SPdL DISTINCTIVES  Mission & Vision Baptism: 

Baptist Beliefs 

We believe that the Holy Spirit empowers local churches to share the Good News of Jesus Christ. To 

that end, we value the “four fragile freedoms” as defined by Baptist historian Walter B. Shurden. 

Christian Practices 

Bible Freedom  Baptists believe that the Bible is a foundational record of God’s revelation to 

humankind. Both individuals and congregations are free to read and interpret the 

Bible under the Lordship of Christ and the leadership of the Holy Spirit. Baptists are 

not beholden to any creeds or reliant on mediators outside of Scripture. 

Soul freedom affirms that each person is created in the image of God and is therefore 

able and responsible—not by force or coercion from a doctrine, clergy or the 

government—for their own direct relationship with God. Baptists believe people may 

only come to Christ on their own volition. Soul freedom is sometimes called the 

“Priesthood of Believers.” 

Soul Freedom 

Church Freedom (or the autonomy of the local church) is the historic belief that local 

churches are free, under the Lordship of Jesus, to determine their membership and 

leadership, to order their worship and work, to ordain whomever they perceive to be 

gifted for ministry (regardless of gender) and to participate in the larger Body of 

Christ (other churches and other denominations). 

Church Freedom 

Religious freedom is the historic Baptist affirmation of freedom OF religion, freedom 

FOR religion, and freedom FROM religion. The earliest Baptists championed the 

separation of church and state in the American colonies and, later, the United States. 

Churches and individuals should be free to worship in whatever manner they choose 

and with whomever they choose. All people, no matter their religious background, 

should be free from any coercion to worship, and free from the intervention of the 

state in matters of religion. 

Religious Freedom 

8

As Baptists, we participate in and perform “believer’s baptism” which means individuals who have 

made a personal decision to follow Jesus are baptized. Our practice is full immersion in water, symbolizing 

the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ. While baptism is important as a public declaration of faith, 

Baptists do not believe it is necessary for salvation. 

The Lord’s Supper:  In Baptist tradition, the Lord’s Supper, or Communion, refers to a symbolic act of worship 

where followers of Christ partake of bread and cup to remember Jesus' death on the cross through the 

symbolism of his broken body and spilled blood. Communion unites us as one body in Christ’s commission 

to continue His ministry. At Second-Ponce, we invite anyone who claims Jesus Christ as their Lord and 

Savior to participate in this ritual. 

# SPdL DISTINCTIVES  Beliefs & Practices Worship at Second-Ponce is a formative hour of hospitality, growth and praise. We 

gather in-person Sundays at 11 a.m. in the Sanctuary, and services are streamed live on 

YouTube. We sing from a hymnal and typically use the New Revised Standard Version 

of the Bible. Periodically, we welcome guest preachers, artistic expressions, orchestra 

music and prayer experiences, all of which add depth to our worship service.

Second-Ponce continues a faithful commitment to missions through financial support

than 12 different organizations and individuals for hands-on ministry and missions 

support. 

Hands-On Service: As Great Commission Christians, it’s important to model God’s 

love through a ministry of presence. This includes hosting mobile food pantries, 

conducting summer camps for underserved neighborhoods and building homes 

through our local Habitat for Humanity. 

# SPdL  MINISTRIES  Ministry Areas Overview SPdL Youth are believers who embrace God, our community and each other by

study, they are becoming young disciples of Christ learning to live out their faith. Our

and pray for each other.

Women’s Fellowship: Women from across our congregation get together at 

someone’s house to unwind, laugh and catch up. 

Young Adults: Includes young professionals, recent college graduates and graduate 

students who meet for Bible study, meals and activities. 

www.spdl.org/children  www.spdl.org/adults  www.spdl.org/youth

In The Kids Club, children grow in faith while exploring God’s love through Bible study, 

prayer, worship and service. Our children’s ministry is: 

Curious |  A place to learn about God’s love. 

Compassionate | A place to care for all God’s creation. 

Cozy | A place to feel safe in the arms of God. 

# SPdL  MINISTRIES  Ministry Areas Overview Benevolence 

In addition to our long-term missions commitments, we maintain supplies for those who come to Second-

Congregational Care is a focused effort to reach out to people in our church family who are in need of 

extra care, including those on our prayer list and those who are not physically able to be with us. 

Second-Ponce has a variety of volunteer service teams aimed at broadening congregational involvement 

while deepening our service to the community. Teams include the flower ministry team, Sunday morning 

greeters, funeral bereavement hosts and a group that prepares the elements for the Lord's Supper. 

A team of volunteer drivers are available during the week to provide non-emergency transportation to 

and from medical appointments.

The Community Wellness Center at Second-Ponce provides a neighborhood space

our church, it is also a full-service gym offering top quality fitness equipment, 

programs and classes. CWC membership rates are lower than most other facilities

Standing Committees 

Standing Committees are groups charged with responsibility for a particular task pertaining to the

determined to be necessary by the Board of Deacons. Membership of the standing committees is to be

Ministry & Leadership Councils 

Second-Ponce's lay ministry leadership is organized around four Ministry Councils: Community, 

Discipleship, Missions and Worship. These councils correspond to Second-Ponce's four core values and 

are overseen by the Deacon Board. Service teams and other programs fall under each of the councils, 

and councils may establish teams/groups to do work on an on-going or ad-hoc basis. The Leadership 

Council brings together the ministers and lay leadership to ensure that all the ministry efforts of the

# SETTING UP  THE FUTURE  Our Next Leader 

Picture of an Ideal Candidate Senior Pastor Position Description | Second-Ponce de Leon Baptist Church 

Overview: The Senior Pastor is the spiritual and administrative leader of the church. He or She is responsible for proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ; teaching Biblical truths through challenging sermons; engaging in pastoral care ministries both within the church and the community; facilitating outreach efforts to new congregants; and for leading collaborative opportunities to grow the church through finances and attendance. 

Status:  Full-time position with a competitive salary, 403(b) retirement contributions, health insurance, long term disability coverage and housing allowance. Additional package benefits include: 

• Paid time off including sick leave and a vacation fund 

• Sabbatical leave 

• Relocation allowances 

• Professional development and continuing education support 

Organizational Relationships: 

• Supervised By : Personnel Committee 

• Supervisory Responsibilities : All Church Staff (Direct Supervision: Ministerial Staff, Administrator) 

• Staff Teams : Ministerial Staff 

• Congregational Teams : Executive Committee and Leadership Council, Ex-officio member of committees 

Essential Job Functions: 

1. Pastoral Leadership 

• Inspire spiritual growth of the congregation through Biblically based sermons, dynamic, Spirit-led worship services and observance of ordinances and Bible teaching. Responsible for pulpit supply when away. 

• Provide vision, leadership, planning and evaluation for the coordinated work of the church. 

• Lead the church in effective programs of Bible study, discipleship, evangelism, outreach, new member assimilation, leadership development and community ministries. • Encourage and model congregational support of local, state, national and international missions through the giving of time, talent, finances and resources. 

• Provide pastoral care through prayer, visitation, funerals, weddings, baby dedications and spiritual counseling. 

• Conduct wedding ceremonies, funeral services and other life rites of passage events as needed with the prerogative of delegating to other staff members when appropriate. 

• Challenge the church to faithful stewardship and ensure the proper use of offerings and income. 

• Represent Second-Ponce through community involvement. 

• Cooperate with other ministry partners in matters of mutual interest and concern. 

• Prepare an annual strategic plan in collaboration with the Leadership Council that includes goals with measurable outcomes as appropriate. 

• Promote harmony within the staff and members of the congregation. 

• Cooperate with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship global office and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship of Georgia, unless the church directs otherwise. 

2. Administrative Leadership 

• Lead and oversee the ministerial staff, coordinate and motivate committees and councils, inspire Deacons and volunteers to serve. 

• Be knowledgeable of and adhere to church bylaws and personnel policies and procedures. 

• Serve ex-officio on all standing boards, committees and councils with the prerogative of delegating to other ministerial staff. 

• Perform other duties that the Personnel Committee and Senior Pastor may agree upon. 

• Recommends, in consultation with the Personnel Committee, additional staff positions and salary adjustments as deemed necessary to accomplish the church mission. 

3. Core Competencies 

• Heart : A heart to serve the Lord and a vibrant relationship with Jesus Christ. 

• Trust & Integrity : Acts and speaks in ways that are direct and truthful; keeps confidence; admits mistakes; is accountable in their commitments; adheres to high ethical standards as well as the core values of the church. • Interpersonal Relationships : Interacts well with others; builds constructive relationships; demonstrates effective communication skills; gives and receives candid feedback; is open to different viewpoints; uses diplomacy and tact; willing to work in a team context when needed. 

• Respectful : Values diverse perspectives; shows sensitivity to individual differences; treats others fairly and with respect; seeks and considers diverse perspectives and ideas. 

• Flexibility & Change : Understands the dynamics of change and the need to build consensus during decision making endeavors; able to adapt to the varying needs of those served. 

• Managing Purpose & Vision : Understands the culture and values of this church; articulates and supports its mission and direction; communicates a compelling and inspired sense of how individuals contribute to the church’s purpose and vision. 

• Conflict Management : Steps up to conflicts, seeing them as opportunities; addresses conflicts by focusing on the issues at hand to develop effective solutions when disputes or disagreements occur; helps others resolve conflicts by providing impartial mediation when needed. 

• Communication : Writes and speaks effectively; demonstrates openness and honesty; listens well during meetings and feedback sessions; explains reasoning behind own opinions; asks others for their opinions; engages stakeholders at the appropriate level of decision making; uses consideration and tact when offering opinions; embraces digital technology. 

• Executive Leadership : Has the willingness and ability to focus on the larger view of the church rather than one’s own area of functional or operational responsibility; can think, reflect, conceptualize and converse on issues of strategic significance to the church's future. 

• Biblical Scholarship : Keeps studying and learning to gain deeper understanding of Scripture; delves into Biblical interpretation, life application and holistic implementation.
